title: Urgent messages and threats
content: Messages that pressure the recipient to act immediately, threaten account closure, or demand sensitive information may be phishing attempts. Urgency alone does not prove a message is malicious, but it is a strong social engineering tactic.
recommended_action: Verify the request through an official channel before taking action.

title: Unexpected links and URLs
content: Unexpected links may lead to fake login pages or harmful websites. A URL can imitate a genuine organization using a misspelled or misleading domain. Avoid clicking unexpected links.
recommended_action: Do not click the link. Visit the organization's official website independently.

title: Requests for passwords or OTPs
content: Requests for passwords, one-time passwords (OTPs), authentication codes, or other confidential information should be treated cautiously, especially when they arrive unexpectedly. Legitimate organizations will rarely ask for credentials via email or text.
recommended_action: Never send passwords or OTPs via email or text. Verify the request using a known, official contact method.

title: What to do after clicking a suspicious link
content: If you clicked a suspicious link and entered a password, immediately change the affected password through the official website or app. If you suspect malware was downloaded, run a security scan and seek trusted technical support.
recommended_action: Change exposed passwords immediately and enable Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA).

title: Impersonation and sender spoofing
content: Attackers often impersonate trusted brands, banks, colleagues, or authority figures to gain trust. They may use a sense of authority to pressure you into performing tasks like buying gift cards or transferring money.
recommended_action: Verify the sender's identity using a different communication channel before acting.
